answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed if it repeats a coordinated, provably false claim, while honest identities recover the stake after a review period. One agent can still lie, but creating an orchard of disposable personas no longer comes free: the attacker must lock capital in every account and risks losing it when evidence links the claims. This raises the cost of flooding an oasis of discussion, though it cannot stop colluding identities that make no slashable claim; saffron is no substitute for the bond.
